message.content: {"thought": "Three fetched sources give specific, quotable evidence on post-learning sleep and procedural memory, including a qualification about pre-sleep performance level.", "action": "finish", "args": {"findings": [{"claim": "In a study with 30-min retention intervals, participants who slept (n=24) or quietly rested (n=22) after learning performed better on a procedural memory task than those who did a distractor task (n=29), with rest and sleep benefits indistinguishable.", "source_id": "W3161707120", "quote": "As hypothesized, sleep and quiet rest both led to better performance on the declarative and procedural memory tasks than did the distractor task.", "stance": "supports"}, {"claim": "In 20 healthy adults, EEG sigma (spindle) power and slow-wave activity during NREM sleep were positively correlated with overnight pre-to-post-sleep consolidation of a procedural mirror-tracing memory task.", "source_id": "W2131973169", "quote": "We found that both electroencephalographic sigma power and slow-wave activity were positively correlated with the pre-post-sleep consolidation of declarative (word list) and procedural (mirror-tracing) memories.", "stance": "supports"}, {"claim": "In children (4-6 y) and adults (18-35 y) performing a motor sequence button-box task, a midday nap produced significant gains in motor skill only at intermediate pre-sleep performance levels, not in low-performing children or high-performing adults.", "source_id": "W1806129265", "quote": "Only at these intermediate performance levels did sleep induce significant gains in motor sequence skill, whereas performance did not benefit from sleep in the low-performing children or in the high-performing adults.", "stance": "supports"}]}}
message.reasoning_content:
We have three sources. Need findings 1-3. Compose claims with exact quotes.

Finding 1: W3161707120 - 30-min post-training sleep vs quiet rest vs distractor; sleep and quiet rest both better than distractor on procedural task; rest indistinguishable from sleep. Quote: "As hypothesized, sleep and quiet rest both led to better performance on the declarative and procedural memory tasks than did the distractor task." Stance: supports (with caveat that sleep not uniquely necessary). Could use stance "supports" since it supports sleep improving procedural memory vs active wake.

Finding 2: W2131973169 - sigma power and slow-wave activity positively correlated with pre-post-sleep consolidation of procedural (mirror-tracing) memory in 20 healthy subjects. Quote: "We found that both electroencephalographic sigma power and slow-wave activity were positively correlated with the pre-post-sleep consolidation of declarative (word list) and procedural (mirror-tracing) memories."

Finding 3: W1806129265 - nap-induced gains in motor sequence skill only at intermediate pre-sleep performance levels; spindle counts correlated with gains in adults. Quote: "Only at these intermediate performance levels did sleep induce significant gains in motor sequence skill, whereas performance did not benefit from sleep in the low-performing children or in the high-performing adults."

Stance: supports (qualified).
